subject: Post-call: performance qualification recap, target SLOs & eval manifest
messages:
From: Alex Martinez <alex@redwood.com>
To: Jenna Lopez <jenna@fastretail.com>, Tom Gray <tom.gray@fastretail.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 9 May 2028 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call: performance qualification recap, target SLOs & eval manifest

Hi Jenna / Tom —

Thanks again for the time today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have a single source of truth as we scope the qualification run. I captured the points we agreed on and some clarifying questions.

Summary of customer targets (captured from call)
- Latency: p95 <= 5.0s for 512-token downstream responses (generation only).
- Throughput: sustained 200 req/sec (peak bursts to 400 req/sec for 30s).
- Concurrency: up to 150 concurrent sessions, each with KV cache warm-up for multi-turn dialogs.
- Streaming: partial token streaming required for the checkout flow (client needs first partial token within 350ms after generation start; then steady streaming at ~50 tokens/sec).
- Accuracy/quality: keep current baseline (we will validate with your prompt set).

Deliverables we will exchange
1) FastRetail -> Redwood: canonical prompt pack + 500-sample prod-like traffic file (you indicated ~5% of real traffic patterns). Please attach any guardrails or deterministic seeds.
2) Redwood -> FastRetail: eval harness (we'll share a Drive folder with harness + a reproducible run plan), the measurement spec (p95, p50, tail, CPU/GPU utilization per token), and an initial run config for two model variants (base FP16 and int8 quantized candidate).
3) Procurement/security: you noted the SOC2 evidence request; send security contact to <security@redwood.com> and we will schedule an evidence handoff.

Open clarifying Qs (please confirm)
- Are the 5s p95 targets intended for cold-start sessions (no KV cache)? We assumed warm sessions but wanted to confirm.
- For streaming: do you require full HTTP/2 streaming or will chunked HTTP SSE (server-sent events) be sufficient for the PoC?
- Do you have an existing test account we can hit for telemetry comparison, or should we use the prod_traffic_sample you provide?

Proposed next steps / timeline
- You: deliver prompt pack + sample traffic by EOD Thu (May 11).
- Us: share eval harness link and proposed run_plan by EOD Fri (May 12).
- Joint: schedule a 2-hour qualification window May 15–17 (please share which day works for your infra/ops).

Attachments: prompt_manifest_v1.csv (prompt taxonomy, token expectations), streaming_sample.jsonl (5 representative streaming sessions)

Thanks — appreciate the alignment. If anything above is off, flag it and we'll adjust.

Best,
Alex Martinez
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
alex@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0193

--
Redwood Inference — Developer-first platform for LLM inference

From: Jenna Lopez <jenna@fastretail.com>
To: Alex Martinez <alex@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>
Cc: Tom Gray <tom.gray@fastretail.com>
Date: Tue, 9 May 2028 15:23:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call: performance qualification recap, target SLOs & eval manifest

Thanks Alex — this is helpful and accurate. A few clarifications and I attached the artifacts we discussed.

Confirmations / clarifications
- Latency: the 5s p95 target is for warm sessions (we expect some prefix/KV caching in production); cold start can be up to 8s for the first few tokens.
- Streaming: HTTP/2 streaming is preferred (we want chunked partial deltas) but SSE is acceptable for the PoC if implementation is simpler. Key requirement: first partial payload to client < 350ms on warm sessions.
- Throughput/Concurrency: our baseline traffic pattern is bursty (holiday peaks) — the sample contains a 30s spike we want you to reproduce. Sustained 200 RPS with bursts to 400 is right.

Attached: FR_prompt_pack_v1.zip (prompt + canonical evaluation rubric), prod_traffic_sample.jsonl (500 events, anonymized).

Procurement: I looped Tom on this email — he will surface the procurement timeline, expecting an initial contract/PO within 3 weeks. Security contact: I copied our infra security lead offline; will share details to security@redwood.com.

We'd like Redwood to run an initial baseline run with our canonical model settings (we'll let you pick the model variant you expect to recommend) and share an artifact we can review. Please include per-request token accounting in the report so we can evaluate cost delta for quantized models.

Thanks —
Jenna
Director, Platform Engineering | FastRetail Inc.
jenna@fastretail.com | +1 (212) 555-2234

Attachments: FR_prompt_pack_v1.zip, prod_traffic_sample.jsonl

From: Alex Martinez <alex@redwood.com>

Date: Tue, 9 May 2028 15:40:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Post-call: performance qualification recap, target SLOs & eval manifest

Folks — forwarding the thread and the artifacts FastRetail just sent. Key asks below and a proposed internal plan.

Key asks from customer
- Validate warm p95 <= 5s for 512-token generation, streaming first-chunk < 350ms.
- Reproduce 30s burst to 400 RPS; sustained 200 RPS.
- Produce per-request token accounting and per-model cost estimate (FP16 vs int8 candidate).

Proposed internal approach
1) Repro harness: use the prod_traffic_sample.jsonl as the canonical traffic source. We should write a harness wrapper that annotates each request with token expectations and simulates client-side streaming behavior.
2) Models to test: - model-A-fp16 (baseline), model-A-int8 (candidate).
3) Measurement spec: p50/p95/p99 latency for first token and full-response, token throughput, GPU util, memory, observed tail behavior. Also record time-to-first-byte for streaming.
4) Repro knobs: fixed random seed, same batch-size schedule, queue depth matching customer concurrency.

Action items (please ack):
- Marissa: put together a run_plan_20280510.md with the harness commands, cluster spec (GPU types/instance counts) and expected run duration. Include reproducibility steps so we can hand the folder to the customer if needed.
- Rishi: map quantization profile for model-A-int8 and estimate delta on tokens/sec and memory.

I'll draft the initial run configs and share the eval harness folder to the FastRetail Drive link once we have the run plan.

Forwarded attachments: FR_prompt_pack_v1.zip, prod_traffic_sample.jsonl

Thanks,
Alex

Ack — thanks for the forward, Alex. I skimmed the prompt pack and the traffic sample. Rishi and I will own the execution and deliverables below.

Commitments and timeline
- Today (May 10): I will publish run_plan_20280510.md to our shared Drive folder (includes testbed spec, dataset prep steps, harness repo commit to use).
- May 11: Rishi will deliver quantization mapping and token-cost delta estimate for model-A-int8.
- May 12: We will run a baseline (model-A-fp16) 1-hour run and capture telemetry; share a reproducible run artifact (logs + perf report).
- May 14: Run candidate int8 profile and provide side-by-side comparison.

Notes for the harness
- Use fixed seed -> put seed=20280510 in harness config to ensure deterministic generation where possible.
- For streaming tests, implement a client that enforces <350ms first chunk and measures inter-chunk time to validate stream shape.
- Include per-request metadata so we can map slow tails to particular prompt groups.

Attachments: run_plan_20280510.md (initial run plan)

I'll add the Drive link to the folder and drop a direct HubSpot update once we have the first baseline artifact.
